facts.statement: Pluridens is an extinct genus of marine lizard classified within the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Pluridens ("many teeth") is an extinct genus of marine lizard belonging to the Mosasauridae.

facts.statement: Pluridens belongs to the subfamily Halisaurinae, which also includes the genera Phosphorosaurus, Eonatator, and Halisaurus.
facts.quote: Pluridens is placed in the subfamily Halisaurinae with the genera Phosphorosaurus, Eonatator and Halisaurus.

facts.statement: Pluridens grew to a size of 5 to 6 meters long, with some individuals possibly exceeding 9 meters.
facts.quote: It also grew large size, measuring 5 - 6 m long and perhaps over 9 m in some individuals.

facts.statement: Some Pluridens specimens show robust jaws with injuries that suggest they engaged in combat.
facts.quote: The jaws in some specimens are robust, and sometimes show injuries suggestive of combat.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Pluridens may have used its jaws to fight over mates or territories.
facts.quote: The jaws may have been used for fighting over mates or territories.

facts.statement: The lower jaws of Pluridens preserve almost twice as many teeth as found in most other mosasaur genera.
facts.quote: dentaries assigned to the genus preserve almost twice the amount of teeth found in most other mosasaur genera.

facts.statement: Lingham-Soliar (1998) compared the lifestyle and feeding habits of Pluridens to early ichthyosaurs like Temnodontosaurus and Leptonectes.
facts.quote: Lingham-Soliar (1998) likened the lifestyle and feeding of Pluridens with that of the ichthyosaurs, particularly early ichthyosaurs such as Temnodontosaurus and Leptonectes.

facts.statement: Lingham-Soliar (1998) noted that Pluridens' unique features would have warranted a new subfamily, but he did not create one due to the fragmentary nature of the fossil remains.
facts.quote: Lingham-Soliar (1998) remarked that the unique combination of features (e.g. the high tooth count and a unique tooth shape) would normally result in the creation of a completely new subfamily, but did not create a new subfamily due to the rather fragmentary nature of the remains.

facts.statement: Lindgren and Siverson (2005) initially reassigned Pluridens walkeri to the genus Halisaurus, but this synonymy was later rejected.
facts.quote: Lindgren and Siverson (2005) considered many of the unique features of Pluridens to be shared with Halisaurus and reassigned P. walkeri as "Halisaurus walkeri".

facts.statement: Pluridens is currently classified as a highly derived member of the Halisaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: Thus, Pluridens is today considered a highly derived halisaurine.

facts.statement: Three species of Pluridens are known: P. walkeri from early Maastrichtian Niger, P. calabaria from Campanian Nigeria, and P. serpentis from late Maastrichtian Morocco.
facts.quote: Three species are known, Pluridens walkeri from the early Maastrichtian of Niger, P. calabaria from the Campanian of Nigeria, and P. serpentis from the late Maastrichtian of Morocco.

facts.statement: A fourth species, Pluridens imelaki, was described in 2026 from Moroccan phosphates based on a single skull and lower jaws.
facts.quote: A fourth species, Pluridens imelaki, was also described from the same phosphates of Morocco in 2026 based on a single skull and associated lower jaws.

facts.statement: Pluridens serpentis, described in 2021 from Morocco, is the most completely known species, represented by two skulls and several jaws.
facts.quote: A third species, Pluridens serpentis, was described from the late Maastrichtian Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco in 2021. It is the most completely known species, being represented by two skulls and a number of jaws.

facts.statement: Some individuals of Pluridens may have reached a size of 8 to 9 meters.
facts.quote: También creció a un tamaño mayor, quizás 8 o 9 metros en algunos individuos.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Pluridens may have used its jaws to fight for mates or territories.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas pueden haber sido utilizadas para pelear por parejas o territorios.

facts.statement: Pluridens was a moderately large mosasaurid approximately 5 meters long.
facts.quote: Pluridens era un mosasáurido moderadamente grande de aproximadamente 5 metros de largo

facts.statement: Pluridens is distinguished by an unusually high number of teeth, separating it from other halisaurines and mosasaurids.
facts.quote: Una característica que separa a Pluridens no solo del resto de los halisaurinos, sino del resto de los mosasáuridos en general es su número inusualmente alto de dientes

facts.statement: The dentary of Pluridens has one of the slimmest profiles among mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Además, el dentario de Pluridens también tiene uno de los perfiles más esbeltos entre los mosasaurios

facts.statement: Because biting force decreases with distance from the jaw joint, the front teeth of Pluridens would have been ineffective for biting and crushing.
facts.quote: Debido a que la fuerza ejercida por el maxilar inferior al morder contra el maxilar superior disminuiría con la distancia desde la articulación, los dientes anteriores habrían sido ineficaces para morder y aplastar

facts.statement: Pluridens is now considered a highly derived halisaurine.
facts.quote: Por lo tanto, Pluridens es ahora considerado como un halisaurino altamente derivado

facts.statement: Lindgren and Siverson (2005) suggested that many unique features of Pluridens are shared with Halisaurus and reclassified P. walkeri as Halisaurus walkeri.
facts.quote: Lindgren y Siverson (2005) consideraron que muchas de las características únicas de Pluridens son compartidas con Halisaurus y reasignaron a P. walkeri como Halisaurus walkeri

facts.statement: Three species have been described: P. walkeri from early Maastrichtian Niger, P. calabaria from Campanian Nigeria, and P. serpentis from late Maastrichtian Morocco.
facts.quote: Se ha descrito a tres especies, Pluridens walkeri del Maastrichtiano temprano de Níger, P. calabaria del Campaniano de Nigeria, y P. serpentis del Maastrichtiano tardío de Marruecos

facts.statement: The type specimen of P. walkeri is BMNH R14153, an almost complete dentary recovered from the Farin-Doutchi Formation near Mount Ilatarda in Niger.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de P. walkeri es BMNH R14153, un dentario casi completo recuperado de la Formación Farin-Doutchi cerca del Monte Ilatarda, en Níger

facts.statement: Longrich (2016) named the new species Pluridens calabaria because the Calabar dentary lacks the extreme lateral bulge and nearly circular dentary section found in BMNH R14153.
facts.quote: El dentario de Calabar además carece del extremo abultamiento lateral y la sección casi circular del dentario y la fuerte expansión transversal de las tecas dentales, ambos rasgos que están presentes en BMNH R14153. Longrich (2016) nombró a la nueva especie Pluridens calabaria

facts.statement: The third species, P. serpentis, was described from Maastrichtian phosphate deposits in Morocco in 2021.
facts.quote: La tercera especie, Pluridens serpentis, fue descrita de los depósitos de fosfatos del Maastrichtiano de Marruecos en 2021

facts.statement: P. serpentis is the species with the most complete known remains, represented by two skulls and several jaws.
facts.quote: Es la especie con restos más completos conocidos, estando representada por dos cráneos y varias mandíbulas

facts.statement: Pluridens lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Pluridens is Pluridensini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Pluridensini

facts.statement: Pluridens belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Mosasauridae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Pluridens is P. walkeri.
facts.quote: Type species: Pluridens walkeri

facts.statement: It is debated whether Pluridens is a distinct genus; Lindgren and Siverson (2005) synonymized it with Halisaurus, but later authors rejected this synonymy.
facts.quote: Lindgren y Siverson (2005) consideraron que muchas de las características únicas de Pluridens son compartidas con Halisaurus y reasignaron a P. walkeri como Halisaurus walkeri. La sinonimia del género fue rechazada por autores posteriores
